summary: After a queued prompt B steers running prompt A, the durable stream emits turn_started for B but the later completion emits turn_ended for A with no acceptance ordinal, so B's announced turn never ends.
GET /api/events returns 400 when after_seq and Last-Event-ID differ, which is what a standard EventSource sends on automatic reconnect after receiving events.

mj events only polls ctrl_c() around response.chunk(), so SIGINT sent while write_all/flush to a stalled stdout pipe is blocked is not acted on, and Tokio's installed handler has disabled default termination.
Title- or project-only search hits now carry no preview, so archived rows from that path lose the preview text in their detail line.
Concurrent model setups share one fixed '.part' path, so one worker can rename another's still-growing file into place and leave a truncated model that later counts as installed.
With an empty cache, the direct-download installer never creates test_wavs, so the ignored end-to-end test always panics at expect("list test_wavs").
The new download title is long, so on narrow terminals the block title cuts off the percentage and the 'Ctrl-R stop' hint.
pin_accepted_codex_model merges only into the override map, so a CODEX_CONFIG exported by the login shell is replaced by a model-only object.
Import uses the local HEAD as base_commit, so unpushed commits produce an empty bundle and restore into a fresh clone cannot check out HEAD.
The Claude import reader never closes a final turn that lacks stop_reason end_turn, so a restored worker replays into Running and rejects prompts.
SSH defaults are put before user ssh_args, but OpenSSH keeps the first value for each option, so user settings such as StrictHostKeyChecking=yes or a longer ConnectTimeout are ignored.
The prepended ConnectTimeout=15 overrides the ConnectTimeout=3 that mount-path completion appends, so Tab completion can block the TUI for about 15 seconds on an unreachable host.
Native import calls collect_git_snapshot without the reject_dirty_submodules guard, so dirty submodule content is silently left out of the archive.
Kimi --latest ranks sessions by the session directory's mtime, which does not change when existing files inside it are appended or rewritten in place.
The new .cargo/config.toml default build target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl breaks the CI jobs that run bare cargo commands with only the host toolchain installed.
The shorthand fallback in github_repository_from_origin makes SCP-style non-GitHub origins such as git@gitlab.com:team/repo.git parse as GitHub owner git@gitlab.com:team.
Kimi --session must be given the session_<uuid> directory name; a bare UUID is not found.
A relative or ~-prefixed destination workspace path could produce the wrong Claude or Kimi native-session key on restore.
kill_if_live skips the group signal once the leader's exit is published, so a backgrounded process with redirected output survives kill, release, shutdown and the drop guard.

The exit status is published only after both pipes reach EOF, so a background child that inherits stdout/stderr keeps terminal/wait_for_exit pending and terminal/output without an exit status after the shell has exited.
Terminal children get the daemon environment plus request env only, not the session's configured environment that the ACP bridge receives.
shell_line puts the command verbatim into sh -c, so a command path with spaces or metacharacters is parsed as shell syntax.
shutdown kills and awaits terminals one at a time with a 5 s timeout each, so teardown time scales with the number of stuck terminals and later groups are signalled late.
Terminals run in their own process groups, so the bare-target daemon stop (a signal to the daemon's group) does not reach them, and the killed daemon runs no Rust teardown.

For an earlier macOS Claude session with a non-default profile home, the link targets the recorded harness_home although Claude actually ran from its default ~/.claude, or creates no link if that path is absent.

After the guard removal, a refreshed launch for a linked legacy macOS Claude session enables subagent_tools, which disables Claude's Agent/Task tools, but the linked home never received the mj-agents MCP configuration.
A legacy session whose recorded profile home directory does not exist gets no link, leaving <worker_root>/profile missing for relaunch and checkpoint.

A legacy worker still running with its old launch.json has project_memory.root under the profile home, but checkpoint now passes <worker_root>/profile as harness_home, so the lexical starts_with check fails.

On a 120 s stall the live Muse helper panics without stopping the runtime, so the test's TempDir (holding the copied auth.json profile) is deleted before the adapter and native Muse process are stopped.
ReviewDispatch::launch requires a hypothesis for each reviewer and then throws it away, so the specialist prompt never contains the risk it was launched to check.
A reminder skipped because a prompt was queued is never reconsidered if that queued prompt is removed, so the idle child reads as owing a report forever.
Queued configuration changes count as pending tasks, so the reminder is skipped, and draining them produces no new turn that would trigger another reminder.

The reminder is submitted unconditionally after async lookups, so a parent follow-up admitted in that window gets an obsolete reminder queued behind it, which can replace the follow-up's valid report.
A handback request that outlives its MCP timeout stays queued, and when it runs later it is attributed to whichever turn is active then, not to the turn that issued it.
A reminder submission whose acknowledgement is lost is recorded as failed even though the worker may have accepted it.
A legacy Row position saved by an older terminal while its prefix was still loading is a tail index, but the new code reads every legacy index as a full-history index and restores the wrong entry.
The new 500 'could not persist logout; retry' response is never shown in the browser, and the in-memory revocation then sends the tab to the login screen, which removes the way to retry.
Logout with a correctly signed but server-expired cookie returns success without recording a revocation, so a renewal response that is still in flight can restore access.
After a restart with a shorter session_ttl, a revocation recorded from an older cookie might expire before a longer-lived cookie issued under the old TTL.
Event streams opened with a cookie before logout keep streaming after the viewer is revoked, because revocation is checked only when the request enters the middleware.
The quota row now wraps to an unbounded number of rows, and on narrow or short terminals that height competes with the input and header for layout space.
Deleting embedded_npm_recipes_match_the_runtime_pins removes the only check that the embedded Codex/Claude package.json files match the runtime pins.
Deleting a_harness_restart_gates_dispatch_until_the_session_is_configured_again drops the only test of the session_configured reset on HarnessRestarting and its reopening on SessionConfigured.
Deleting daemon_restart_without_a_baseline_does_not_hide_pending_work removes the only test of the restart branch that must not create a fresh review baseline.
apply_worker_summary replaces the summarized unread count but keeps unread_agent_message_sequences that the new summary already counts, so a reconnect double-counts unread messages.
Summary hydration counts unread messages for the selected, expanded session, which the event path deliberately treats as read.
Poll targets keep the viewed_through value captured before the user read a conversation, so a later reconnect's summary brings back unread badges for messages already read.
With the bounded 10-entry tail, a session whose last assistant text is outside the tail looks empty, so Delete force-destroys it with no typed confirmation and no checkpoint.

When the dashboard opens a protocol-3 session, the full replay moves the client cursor past events that recovery never observes, so an automatic recovery checkpoint for a completed turn can be missed.

Worker source pinning now runs before the daemon publishes its endpoint, so slow copying can exceed the client's 8-second START_TIMEOUT and make the launching command fail although the daemon is healthy.
Each distinct local worker build is copied into a permanent digest directory under data_dir/workers/pinned and nothing ever removes old ones, so disk use grows with every rebuild and restart.
A cached artifact keeps the permission mode of its first capture, so a source that was not executable stays non-executable in the cache after the source is fixed.
`mj go` in a folder named `default`, while the built-in default workspace is empty, tries to create `default` and is refused.

The new refusal prints each workspace's session_count as 'N sessions', but that count excludes stopped and lost sessions, so a newly listed default holding only suspended history shows '(0 sessions)'.
`mj new` reads the prompt and checks --bundle/--project-directory before it checks for a workspace, so a command missing several arguments reports the other error first.
A renamed default workspace becomes hidden when it has no sessions, and its new name is then refused for creation.

A session/new that is admitted but then fails or times out in the new readiness wait leaves its id in `sessions`, so unanswered_refusal() suppresses the refusal and `mj acp` exits 0 although no session/new succeeded.

Raising the shutdown_all_kills_running_terminal_commands wait from 5 s to 60 s lets the test pass when shutdown_all fails to kill the process, because the 30 s sleep/ping exits on its own before the deadline.
The rename dialog renders Field focus and Save focus identically, so after tabbing to Save the user cannot see that typing is now ignored.
A checkpoint that defers after the prestage leaves its uniquely named checkpoint-stage directory on the target; only the pack step removes it, so repeated deferrals pile up full copies.

An idle observation that arrives while a deferred copy is still registered as busy is consumed, and clearing last_attempted_turn afterwards does not schedule a retry, so the due boundary can stay uncopied.

If a prompted turn ends and a self-started harness turn begins before the review host sees an Idle view, the watch is overwritten with prompt_driven=false and the prompted turn never arms an automatic review.

A deferred manual checkpoint persists last_checkpoint_error = None because the field was cleared at the start of the attempt and the deferral branch does not restore the previous value, so an earlier checkpoint warning is erased.

The 15-second SAVE_ACK_TIMEOUT applied to the profile/target rename also covers the local blocking configuration reload, so a slow reload after a successful rename is reported as an unacknowledged save and its result is discarded.

muse_data_dir decides whether a profile home is the person's own Muse home by lexical path equality, so a symlinked or otherwise aliased path to ~/.config/muse looks for the catalog under <home>/.data/muse and finds none.

The clean login environment drops the Rust base image's ENV RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME, and the new profile.d script does not restore them, so rustup in container sessions looks under /home/hel/.rustup instead of the preinstalled toolchain.

The worker's clean re-exec drops the GH_TOKEN that provisioning injects into the container environment, so configure_github_cli never writes the session token file and early gh/Git operations lack credentials until credential sync runs.

run_inner (and the supervisor) re-merge the cached login environment under the prepared spec, restoring GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE variables that configure_github_cli deliberately moved into the worker-owned gitconfig.
ACP terminal spawn removes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN after applying the request's explicit environment.
Clearing the worker environment drops SSH_AUTH_SOCK, so SSH-remote pushes and Git operations that depend on an ssh-agent or forwarded agent fail on bare targets.
For worker push-branch and diff, the clean re-exec drops the container target's configured environment, because only Run and PrepareHarness re-apply target_environment.
The mandatory login capture runs '<shell> -l -c script', which csh/tcsh reject, so workers for C-shell accounts fail to start.

On SshBare and AwsEc2 targets, the controller records a relative dispatcher command, while the worker compares it with an absolute worker root, so the owned review dispatcher is never recognized and is not preapproved.
The new failed-session dialog prints the full error in a non-scrolling paragraph, so a long error or short terminal clips the action buttons below the popup.

The cancellation gate reads the daemon's cached controller, which is not synchronized with the close task that persists Destroying through its own Controller, so Alt-X can still cancel target teardown after the point of no return.
active_lifecycles now locks self.controller, but session_projection already holds that non-reentrant std Mutex when it calls active_lifecycles, so the web feed deadlocks the daemon.

A Stop retry routed to recover_interrupted_close_managed can move Closing to Destroying, clear last_error, and then fail without recording the error, so the TUI treats the record as an in-progress transition and blocks Stop again.
The new close-failure recovery dialog has no production caller, and the diff removed the dashboard's `x` force-destroy key, so force destroy cannot be reached from the dashboard.

The lossy annotation makes cross-harness profile choices wrap, but render_picker sizes the popup by choice count and does not scroll, so later choices and help text can be clipped while still selectable.

The new post-stop check pipes `ps -eo args=` into `grep -F -- "$hel_match"`, and the concurrently running grep's own argv contains the expanded match, so the check can report a surviving worker after a successful stop.
A running session with a failed review whose worker becomes unreachable is classified Unreachable instead of Failed, which contradicts the new Failed > Unreachable ladder.
notification_body has no Unreachable arm, so a desktop notification for an unreachable worker shows the last agent message or "Finished" instead of a connectivity failure.
The wide minimized Sessions title shows only "Attention: N" without the most-urgent glyph, while the compact forms and other badges include it.
delete_empty_workspace_at allows deleting the 'default' workspace, after which every session-context insert that relies on the column default fails the new trigger with 'unknown workspace'.
The added fourth session_contexts column breaks existing tests that do positional three-value inserts on a migrated or fresh database.

version_thirteen_restores_checkpointed_lost_sessions_to_recoverable_errors resets user_version to 12 on a database that already has the version-14 objects, so reopening fails at CREATE TABLE workspaces.
Unicode lowercasing can lengthen name_key beyond 64 characters, so names that pass normalize_workspace_name fail the name_key CHECK constraint.
assign_new_session_workspace_at cannot tell a newly created context from an existing default-workspace session, so it can move existing sessions.
assign_new_session_workspace_at reads the current workspace and updates it on separate statements outside a transaction, so two concurrent assignments of the same session can both succeed.
owner_only_create_options binds `let mut options` but only mutates it under #[cfg(unix)], so Windows Clippy with -D warnings fails on unused_mut.

The worker root is already created with default modes by provisioning (mkdir -p) before the worker runs, so WorkerRootOwner::acquire's owner-only creation has no effect for newly provisioned sessions.
A prompt submitted while a config update is in flight is discarded with only a warning, leaving the UI in Streaming state forever with the prompt lost.
refresh_config_picker keeps only clamped numeric indices, so a config update that removes or reorders options while the value picker is open can retarget the picker to a different option or value.
Picker height is rows + 4 while the borders, header and footer need 5 rows, which is claimed to leave no room for the list when there is a single option or value.
Pointer hit testing lets controls registered after an expanded combobox win over its visible popup, so clicks and wheel events on popup rows go to the covered field or button.

Ctrl-S while a Setup scalar choice popup is open closes the combobox through route() but Save is ignored, leaving a collapsed choice editor that Enter or a click cannot reopen and that Esc turns into closing Setup.
Accepting a Code review selector without changing its value closes the combobox internally but does not request a repaint, so the popup stays on screen.

An open Model or Effort combobox keeps a numeric pending index when capability discovery replaces the option list, so the highlighted option and the value Enter commits can shift to a different choice.
When one dashboard closes the default workspace, other connected dashboards skip composer disposal because only the initiating client receives the explicit deletion response.
If the workspace close commits but the follow-up runtime_snapshot or workspace-list request fails, the dashboard reports the whole close as failed and never runs the deleted-workspace cleanup.
Workspace draft disposal does not clear DashboardState::standby_prompts, so standby composer text typed during an attach can come back when the preserved session is reopened.

The pinned field title is drawn as a single unwrapped row, so a title wider than the pane (or containing a newline) is clipped and its remainder, including a trailing ' (required)', cannot be read anywhere.

Bundle export reads the checkpoint's committed bundle, but a managed-worktree checkpoint is a DeltaFrom the worktree's current HEAD, so the bundle is always empty and the endpoint always refuses with 'no commits beyond the session base' even after the session commits.
An unmanaged bare checkout's checkpoint is metadata-only, so bundle export is refused for it.
Claims managed network workspace bundles exclude all origin refs, so pushing the session branch empties the bundle.
File reads for bare sessions are bounded by the project directory's parent, so a caller can read sibling files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or sibling worktrees.
Bare-session file reads resolve paths against the project's parent, so ordinary project-relative paths resolve in the wrong directory (and the boundary is one level too wide).
An unmanaged bare checkout sends neither --base nor --branch, so the diff endpoint fails with 'no session base recorded'.
For a session whose project is a subdirectory of its checkout, the diff stages only `.` into an empty scratch index, so files outside the subdirectory appear deleted against the full base tree.
The session diff decodes git's patch with from_utf8_lossy, so text files with non-UTF-8 bytes produce a corrupted patch.
Capturing into an empty scratch index with `git add -A` skips tracked files that match an ignore rule, so the diff reports them as deleted.

When the adapter reloads through session/load and the load fails with a missing Codex thread, the new fallback to session/new never turns session_updates_enabled on, so every update from the replacement thread is dropped.

Snapshots written before native_session_used existed read it as false, and the earlier SessionOpened{resumed:true} or imported identity is never re-applied, so a previously resumed or imported thread can be classified as unused and replaced.
A successful resume marks the thread used durably, but the in-process native_session_used atomic stays false, so a bridge restart in the same worker can still allow replacement.
The controller's GitHub token is placed in podman/container/ssh argv as --env GH_TOKEN=<token>, where other local users can read it from process listings.
use_github_https_urls uses a parser that treats any two-part string as owner/repo shorthand, so non-GitHub SCP URLs like git@gitlab.com:team/repo get rewritten to github.com.

The container bootstrap now always installs gh when it is missing, even with no token or no GitHub repositories, so non-root images that have git but not gh (including the previous bundled image) fail to provision.

The runtime task records Failed directly while SessionStarted still travels through the orchestrator, so a session that starts and then exits quickly is recorded as a launch failure, and first-outcome-wins makes that permanent.
begin() evicts the oldest record even if it is still Starting, so 64 newer launches during one slow startup make the waiting viewer get 404s and fall back to a timeout instead of the real failure.

In Recover mode, a corrupt terminated line longer than RELAY_EVENT_BYTE_BUDGET makes read_bounded_line return an error before the new skip branch runs, so the whole scan aborts instead of recording a gap and continuing.
Claims the new Recover variant and RelayJournalGap fields are dead code in the library build, so clippy -D warnings fails.
A model or effort chip that only partly fits is still drawn with chip styling, but no hitbox is registered, so clicking the visible part does nothing.

During a running turn the right-aligned activity spinner overwrites the last cells of the left title, but chip_limit reserves no space for it, so spinner cells can stay clickable as a model or effort chip.

review_refs_metadata_only is set only when refs/mj refs exist, so a raw metadata-only capture without them is restored as a full snapshot and can check out the old commit in the user's shared checkout.
Claims an older Mjolnir would accept a schema-10 archive, ignore the new flag, and fail on missing ref objects, so the format change needs a version bump.

A prompt that first arrives while the record already says running but before the first worker report sets capabilities.prompt is still refused with 409, because the first loop pass uses is_coming_up, which accepts only Provisioning or Disconnected.
The up-to-60-second readiness wait holds no upgrade admission, so a daemon handoff can end the HTTP request before the prompt is submitted.
The TUI chat now receives only a 1,024-item transcript window from the dashboard poller, so scrollback before the window is no longer reachable and entries drop out as the window advances.

Dashboard unread agent-message and restart counts are rebuilt from the windowed transcript only, so unread items before the window are dropped and the counts from startup summary hydration are overwritten.
When one turn exceeds 1,024 items, the dashboard's last-user preview and the agent activity shown after it disappear, because the detail still scans the windowed transcript for the last user message.

The SQL-derived latest_user_position skips user items with empty visible text while ProjectionWindow::of and the old latest_completed_turn_ordinal count every user item, so the recovery observer could see a stale turn.
The review host's seed would lose the original task and earlier user prompts because it receives the truncated projection.
The browser transcript could show fewer than 1,000 visible lines, or none, because raw_only entries are filtered after the 1,024-item window is applied.
The COUNT(*) used for omitted_items still costs work proportional to the session's history on every poll.
At phone widths with an empty composer, Tab from the editor into Send/Attach removes composer-has-intent and hides the toolbar holding the newly focused button.
Claim: the outer #conversation-side 25dvh/overflow rule nests a second scroller around the new 40dvh inner region on phones.
phone-layout.spec.js sets isMobile:true unconditionally, which Playwright rejects for Firefox, breaking the MJ_BROWSER_ENGINE=firefox configuration that playwright.config.js supports.
mj resume --wiki <native-id> --json prints import progress to stdout before the JSON object, so stdout is not valid JSON.
The import branch ignores the indexed path and searches only the stock harness home, so sessions indexed from a non-default profile home cannot be continued, or the wrong same-ID session is imported.
The native import branch hardcodes allow_dirty_local/allow_omitted_non_git to false and ResumeArgs has no such flags, so a noninteractive caller cannot acknowledge import safety warnings.
The archived-restore branch sends workspace_id None, which the route turns into an empty string and never resolves, so restoration without --workspace-id fails session record validation.

Archived container/bundle sessions index an empty project, and the CLI restore always sends project_directory None with no flag to supply one, so restore_wiki_session fails with 'name a project directory'.

Local path completion runs synchronous read_dir/is_dir that ignore the 5-second deadline and cancellation, so a stalled local filesystem keeps a shared preflight slot (cap 4) indefinitely, even after the browser disconnects.
ArrowUp/ArrowDown change only aria-selected and never scroll the 40dvh suggestion list, so the highlighted row can be off-screen when Enter accepts it.
The suggestion rows are default-tabbable buttons, so Tab from the path input targets a row that the input's blur handler deletes, and focus is lost instead of moving to the next field.

When the source adapter supports session/resume but not session/load, the runtime resumes without replaying history and still emits SessionStarted{resumed:true}, so the import exits at once with an empty handoff and reports that there was no transcript.

A prompt typed while the temporary import session is replaying is queued to the source runtime, which the UI shuts down right after SessionStarted. The request may start on the source agent and is cut off, and the destination is told to acknowledge and wait.

resolve_repository wraps every error from resolve_local_repository in a precondition Refusal, so Git execution failures, timeouts, cancellation and unreadable paths become a 409 telling the caller to configure a remote, with no log reference.
When the capacity poller channel is closed, the reply names daemon-log reference `capacity-poller`, but the warning logged on that path does not contain that reference.
same_installation now calls std::fs::canonicalize, and Settings runs setup_additions on the TUI event loop, so a slow or hung profile-home filesystem freezes the dashboard after Detect profiles.
Treating a `~` home as equal to its absolute form suppresses the absolute duplicate while other consumers still read `~` literally.
A missing component plus `..` after a symlinked prefix makes the lexical fallback keep the symlink, so a duplicate profile is still added.
When canonicalize fails, the lexical fallback collapses `link/..` as if link were a plain directory, so a configured home can falsely match a different discovered home and suppress it.
Every spawn now sends a model in the start follow-up, and a Muse child's live session has no model selector, so the follow-up rejects the synthesized model and the child never gets its prompt.

Explicit and inherited efforts are checked against the chosen profile's default-model effort list, not the requested model's list, so valid efforts are rejected and invalid inherited efforts make the child's start fail.

spawn(model: "current") reads only operational.config, which has no model entry for a parent that never changed its model, so it fails as 'current model is unknown'. A default effort is not inherited either.
spawn now waits on every candidate profile's discovery, which can outlast the 120-second MCP shim reply timeout, so the parent gets a tool error while the daemon may still create the child.
adopt_restarted_checkpoint_relay falls back to an unleased standalone connection when the post-restart lease fails, so the checkpoint/close runs without the actor's exclusive reservation.

After the initial lease fails, the actor stays unleased during the worker restart, so a prompt submitted then reaches the restarted worker and blocks or is interrupted by the Stop barrier, and restarted_worker prevents a retry.

The actor and the restart's StandaloneSession both apply relay events to the same stored projection, and adoption replaces the actor's freshly synced connection with the older standalone one, so a later sync hits AlreadyApplied and aborts Stop.

If the proxy exits before the hello frame is written, call_hello fails with 'write relay hello request: Broken pipe', which worker_connect_needs_restart does not match, so Stop does not restart the dead worker.

The summary SQL uses one-argument trim(), which removes only spaces, so agent messages that contain only newlines or tabs count as unread and can be chosen as the last message, which then renders as None.
The startup summary's unread count is computed from the read cursor captured at startup and applied unconditionally, so a session read before the summary arrives becomes unread again.
last_materialized_user_message only considers items whose stable_id starts with 'user:' or 'user-', so user items with other IDs are skipped.

The native-restore seed reads only the literal keys `model` and `effort` from the archived projection, which stores selectors under the harness's advertised option IDs, so an effort advertised as `reasoning_effort` (Codex) is dropped on resume.

The seed takes model and effort from the projection, which holds the bridge's advertised current values (including provider defaults never chosen), instead of the relay's accepted configuration, so a resume pins an old default as if the user had chosen it.

The launch config carries only the marker's file name, so Kimi's `credentials/kimi-code.json` (and ZCode's `v2/config.json`) becomes a file at the home root and credential sync reads and writes a file the harness never uses.

A 2xx catalog response is cached before it is parsed, so an invalid body replaces the last good catalog, fails the current launch without trying the cached copy, and poisons the fallback for later outages.
Catalog rows and default-model discovery rows share the `(profile, "")` primary key in profile_config_cache, so each overwrites the other despite different fingerprints.
The new mandatory catalog step accepts only Codex's `{"models": [...]}` shape, so a custom provider whose `/models` returns the OpenAI-standard `{"data": [...]}` list cannot launch.

A custom provider that inlines `experimental_bearer_token` gets no staged catalog, and profile validation forbids a user-supplied `model_catalog_json`, so the profile keeps OpenAI's built-in model names with no way to fix it.
Quota for a ZCode profile now always returns 'no longer supported' while the ZCode harness is still enabled.
The catalog fallback expires after 24 hours because it reuses profile_config_cache's staleness window.
For a legacy worker that does not lead its own process group, KILL escalation sends SIGKILL to the worker's inherited process group, bypassing the hel_group=legacy single-PID safeguard.
A descendant that starts a new process group after the one-time snapshot is not tracked, so the stop can report success and the rm can race that live writer.
A failed ps in the snapshot is treated as an empty tree, so the stop silently falls back to waiting for the leader group only and can authorize removal.
hel_kill_tree signals snapshotted PIDs and PGIDs without checking process identity, so a PID or PGID reused during the grace period could be killed.

Typing a palette query keeps the cursor on the previously selected command (often the Recent head) when it still matches as a subsequence, so Enter runs a command other than the top match, such as Stop session.
When an active Sessions filter excludes a newly created session, select_active_session refuses it, so creation leaves the previous session selected while focus moves to the prompt.

When the filter hides every row, the pinned Create/Resume action row takes focus, and the guard `session_action_focus.is_none()` then stops Esc and the state letters from clearing the filter, although the empty pane says 'Esc clears the filter'.
Filtering prunes the folded state of hidden projects, because clamp_selections keeps collapsed keys only for projects in the now-filtered project_keys, so clearing the filter expands them.
Pasting while editing the Sessions search does nothing, because handle_paste ignores every focus except Prompt.
Commands with pane keys, such as Create session and Search sessions, are never added to Recent even when run from the palette.
Once failures have stacked, the bar text holds the formatted count, so a repeat of the latest failure compares unequal and increments the count even though the log skips the duplicate.
In ASCII mode the composer hints are split on " - " but the composer_keys literals still use " · ", so the hints become one item that keeps Unicode and is dropped as a whole when space is short.
truncate_line_to_width reserves one cell for the ellipsis, but the ASCII ellipsis is two cells, so truncated output is one cell wider than requested.
In ASCII mode a partial cell under one half draws nothing, but empty_cells still subtracts a cell for it, so the quota bar is nine cells instead of ten.
The transcript (and second-opinion) row caches are not keyed on the symbol set, so changing Symbols in Setup leaves existing rows drawn with the old glyphs.
The Recent messages log truncates each notice to one row with no wrap or other way to read the rest, so long failures cannot be recovered.
The stacked-failure notice hard-codes the Unicode middle dot, so ASCII mode still shows it.
Several conversation render paths still emit hard-coded Unicode (voice button glyph, middle dots, "Listening…") in ASCII mode, contrary to the commit's claim that every glyph comes from the table.
Answering a turn-review form calls poll_turn_review_role, which starts a second self-rescheduling poll loop for a role that already has one, so each answer adds a permanent loop.

After a turn-review form is answered, nothing marks it in flight, so a poll that returns before the resolution is journaled makes surface_reviewer_elicitations reopen the same form, and the reopened dialog is never dismissed.
A tight nested list merges the parent item's text into the child's line and loses the parent bullet, because the parent's buffered spans are not flushed before the child item overwrites item_prefix.
Rich mode drops Markdown link destinations (including those generated for ACP ResourceLink blocks), so the URL cannot be seen or opened without switching to raw mode.
Table rows are joined without padding cells to a common column width, so column separators do not line up across rows.
A header-only table wider than the viewport renders nothing, because the record fallback skips the header row and there are no data rows.
Worker recovery and parked sub-agent wake compare the digest of the image worker (through the hel link) with the host worker, which differs in bytes, and copy the host worker over the link.
The ignored Docker integration test assumes agent-dev:latest has no worker, but this change publishes :latest with one, so its first assertion fails against the new image.
A dangling symlink at /opt/mjolnir/mj-worker makes the probe report 'absent' because test -e follows links, so the host worker is installed instead of reporting an unusable image worker.
